utility.notes: Ava Community Energy's own Berkeley page confirms PG&E's continued role as the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility, stating the Renewable 100 default product 'costs an additional 1¾ cent per kilowatt-hour above PG&E rates' and that customers may 'return to PG&E service.' Ava is a separate default generation supplier layered on top of PG&E delivery — see generation_supplier.

value.name: Ava Community Energy - Renewable 100 (default for most residential customers) / Bright Choice (automatic for CARE, FERA, and Medical Baseline customers)
value.notes: Per Ava Community Energy's own Berkeley page: 'In June 2021, the Berkeley City Council voted to set the default electricity option for Berkeley residents (except those on CARE, FERA, and/or Medical Baseline rates) to Ava's Renewable 100 service starting in March 2022... residential customers on the CARE, FERA, or Medical Baseline programs automatically remain on Bright Choice.' This is a different default product than the Fremont record's (Bright Choice) — a genuine per-city council decision, not an inconsistency.

city.notes: Given as the run's input parameter; confirmed by the City of Berkeley's own official site.

county.notes: Berkeley Municipal Code's own definitions section (BMC 1.04.010) states: '"County" means the county of Alameda, California,' directly confirming the jurisdiction relationship on the city's own code, hosted at berkeley.municipal.codes.

permit_authority.value: City of Berkeley Permit Service Center (Building & Safety Division)

interconnection_url.notes: Same PG&E-wide Net Energy Metering program URL already verified for the Fremont, Oakland, San Jose, Fresno, and Stockton records — reused here as a utility-level fact (PG&E's NEM program page is the same for every city in its distribution territory, not city-specific). pge.com has returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch in every prior check this session; the URL is confirmed to exist on PG&E's official domain via search engine indexing under its expected title.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Berkeley/Alameda County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program and figures already verified for the Fremont/Oakland/San Jose records this session, reused here because SGIP is administered per IOU distribution territory (PG&E), not per city — PG&E's distribution role in Berkeley is independently confirmed via S5. Re-check against selfgenca.com's live Program Metrics page before showing as current. Removed the previously-listed "SGIP - Equity Resiliency" line item on 2026-08-09: its expires_on (2025-12-31) has definitively elapsed and no renewal/replacement was confirmed this session, so it no longer represents a current program; the remaining item(s) here are still active/unknown-status per their own status field.

Schematic Site Plan (property lines, PV system location, main electrical panel/subpanels, equipment and disconnect locations)
Electrical Plan (single line diagram of PV and utility interconnect, conductor/raceway specifications)
Roof Plan and Cross-Section (roof layout, module attachment, fire-safety access pathways and labeling)
value.required_when: always, standard (non-streamlined) submittal; stamped engineering calculations additionally required if roof framing exceeds allowable span/spacing limits or panels are not flush-mounted

value.name: Manufacturer's Specification Sheets (make, model, listing, size, weight for inverters, panels, racks, combiner boxes)

required_documents.notes: From the City of Berkeley Building & Safety Division's 'Solar Photovoltaic (PV) System Submittal Requirements' document. This document explicitly applies to the standard submittal path — it directs streamlined-eligible projects (10kW AC or less, single-family/duplex) to a separate 'Solar PV Residential Requirements for Streamlined Review' document, which was not located/fetched this session, so streamlined-path requirements are not separately verified here.

value: Final inspection required after installation and before the solar system is granted final approval
Inspections may be scheduled through Permits Online, the automated phone scheduling system at (844) 216-2170, or by phone at (510) 981-7440 (option 1)

value.notes: Berkeley's Solar Permits page states 'Projects submitted under the standard permit process will be reviewed within one working day.' The Building & Safety Division's submittal-requirements document separately states 'Allow 5 working days for review of plans with calculations' — i.e. specifically when stamped structural engineering calculations are required (non-flush-mounted panels, or roof framing exceeding standard span/spacing limits). No specific timeline is stated for SolarAPP+ real-time or Permits Online streamlined applications.

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined solar permitting (Permits Online) / SolarAPP+ real-time permitting
other_conditions: Must mark all items 'Yes' on the Eligibility Checklist for Solar Streamlining to use the streamlined process; SolarAPP+ has its own separate eligibility checklist referenced on the same page.

eligibility_constraints.notes: The 10kW AC cap and single-family/duplex scope are stated for the streamlined (Permits Online) pathway specifically: 'small solar rooftop system (10kW AC or less)' on 'single family or duplex home.' SolarAPP+'s own eligibility checklist is referenced but not itself detailed on this page, so its criteria are not separately verified here.

permit_fees.notes: Berkeley's Solar Permits page states only that the city 'encourages the installation' through 'minimal permit fees,' without a specific dollar figure — not detailed enough to record as a verified fee.
